graphEvents.label: Can a model start a slash command itself on each runtime
Six runtimes mirror commands; Devin has no command surface

label: Six runtimes mirror the command tree into a user-facing slash surface: 45 Claude files, symlinked OpenCode groups, 46 Cursor files, 45 Codex prompts, 46 Pi prompts and 45 DSH prompts; Devin has agents, hooks, skills and repo-rules but no commands or prompts directory.
The command tree defines commands as user-invoked slash commands, each a markdown file with YAML frontmatter and allowed tools, and names no model-callable surface.

AGENTS.md Gate 2 tells the model to use the hook brief or run the advisor CLI and emit SKILL ROUTING; Gate 4 names command-spec-kit as a tiebreak, and neither instructs the model to type a slash command.
The advisor outage fallback prints a shell command for the model to run, which is a precedent for model-executed shell entry points but not for slash commands.
A command file is a thin router over repository markdown and YAML, so a model that can read files and run tools can execute its workflow without runtime slash expansion.

Two fallbacks cover every runtime: name the command and ask the user to type it, which needs a slash surface, or load the command document and follow its workflow, which works on all seven runtimes including Devin.

Delivery is not the constraint: the advisor delivers a brief on seven runtimes through one renderer while command mirrors exist on six; the missing piece is a model-callable command entry, not a context channel.

direction: Give the model the slash string and it will invoke it
reason: Command docs are user-invoked, no tool schema exposes a slash command, and no model-facing rule instructs typing one
